chunks.title: How to Sign In — How to Sign In [#how-to-sign-in]
chunks.text:
How to Sign In [#how-to-sign-in]


SGI has two ways to sign in. They both give you access to the same features, with some [documented exceptions](#whats-different-between-the-two). Choose the one that works best for you.

chunks.title: How to Sign In — Steam Sign-in [#steam-sign-in]
chunks.text:
Steam Sign-in [#steam-sign-in]


This is the recommended method. SGI signs in directly to Steam's servers so it doesn't need the Steam client installed or running on your PC at all.

<Callout type="info">
  SGI never sees or stores your password. Your information is sent directly to Steam's own servers to establish the sign-in, the same as signing in through the official Steam client or mobile app
</Callout>

<Steps>
  <Step>
    ### Open SGI [#open-sgi]

    On first launch, you'll land on the sign-in screen
  </Step>

  <Step>
    ### Choose Steam Sign-in [#choose-steam-sign-in]

    Click <MockButton type="steam-sign-in" />
  </Step>

  <Step>
    ### Sign in [#sign-in]

    * Enter your Steam **username and password**, or
    * Use the <MockButton type="qr-sign-in" /> panel shown next to it, and scan the code with the Steam mobile app
  </Step>

  <Step>
    ### Steam Guard [#steam-guard]

    If prompted, approve the sign-in from your Steam mobile app, or enter the Steam Guard code sent to your email
  </Step>

  <Step>
    ### Continue [#continue]

    Once signed in, you're taken straight to the dashboard automatically
  </Step>
</Steps>

chunks.title: How to Sign In — Legacy Sign-in [#legacy-sign-in]
chunks.text:
Legacy Sign-in [#legacy-sign-in]


Use this if you'd rather not enter your Steam username/password into SGI at all. It requires the Steam client to already be installed, running, and signed in.

<Callout type="warning">
  You must have the [Steam client](https://store.steampowered.com/about) installed, running, and signed in to at least one account
</Callout>

<Callout type="info">
  Legacy Sign-in only supports one signed-in account at a time. This is a real limitation of the Steam client itself, not something SGI can lift. To use more than one account at once, sign in to the additional accounts with [Steam Sign-in](/docs/get-started/how-to-sign-in#steam-sign-in) instead
</Callout>

<Steps>
  <Step>
    ### Install Steam [#install-steam]

    Download and install the [Steam client](https://store.steampowered.com/about)
  </Step>

  <Step>
    ### Sign in to Steam [#sign-in-to-steam]

    Sign in to your Steam account via the Steam client
  </Step>

  <Step>
    ### Choose Legacy Sign-in [#choose-legacy-sign-in]

    Open SGI and click <MockButton type="legacy-sign-in" /> on the sign-in screen
  </Step>

  <Step>
    ### Select your account [#select-your-account]

    If you're signed in to more than one account in the Steam client, SGI lists all of them; choose yours by clicking its avatar
  </Step>

  <Step>
    ### Continue [#continue-1]

    Click <MockButton type="continue" /> to proceed to the dashboard
  </Step>
</Steps>

chunks.title: How to Sign In — What's different between the two [#whats-different-between-the-two]
chunks.text:
What's different between the two [#whats-different-between-the-two]


SGI behaves differently depending on which method you used to sign in. This is because each method talks to and interacts with Steam in a different way. The table below summarizes the differences:

|                            | **Steam Sign-in**                                         | **Legacy Sign-in**                                             |
| -------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Steam client required?     | No                                                        | Yes, must be installed, running, and signed in                 |
| Sign-in method             | Steam username/password, or QR code sign-in               | Pick from accounts already signed in to the local Steam client |
| Multiple accounts at once? | Yes, see [Multi-Account](/docs/get-started/multi-account) | No, one account at a time                                      |
| Play games while idling?   | No                                                        | Yes                                                            |

Everything else (Card Farming, Achievement Unlocker, Achievement Manager, Inventory Manager, Idling, Automatic Idler, Favorites) works the same regardless of which method you used.

chunks.title: Installation Guide — Install [#install]
chunks.text:
Install [#install]


SGI supports **Windows** (10/11, 64-bit) and **Linux** (64-bit). Follow the steps below for your OS and install method.

chunks.title: Installation Guide — Windows Installer [#windows-installer]
chunks.text:
Windows Installer [#windows-installer]


<Steps>
  <Step>
    ### Download [#download]

    Download `Steam.Game.Idler_X.X.X_x64-setup.exe` from the [latest release](https://github.com/zevnda/steam-game-idler/releases/latest/) page on GitHub
  </Step>

  <Step>
    ### Install [#install-1]

    Run the installer and follow the steps of the installation guide
  </Step>

  <Step>
    ### Run [#run]

    After installation, you can launch SGI in a few different ways:

    * Select "Run Steam Game Idler" and click "Finish" when prompted
    * Run `Steam Game Idler.exe` from the installation directory
      * Defaults to `C:/Program Files/Steam Game Idler`
    * Use the desktop shortcut created by the installer
  </Step>
</Steps>

chunks.title: Installation Guide — Windows Portable [#windows-portable]
chunks.text:
Windows Portable [#windows-portable]


<Callout type="warn">
  The portable version does not support automatic updates. You'll need to download and replace the executable manually for each new release
</Callout>

<Steps>
  <Step>
    ### Download [#download-1]

    Download `Steam.Game.Idler_X.X.X_x64-portable.zip` from the [latest release](https://github.com/zevnda/steam-game-idler/releases/latest/) page on GitHub
  </Step>

  <Step>
    ### Extract [#extract]

    Extract the contents of the `.zip` file to any folder you want
  </Step>

  <Step>
    ### Run [#run-1]

    Open the folder and run `Steam Game Idler.exe`
  </Step>
</Steps>

chunks.title: Installation Guide — Linux [#linux]
chunks.text:
Linux [#linux]


<Callout type="info">
  Linux supports [Steam Sign-in](/docs/get-started/how-to-sign-in#steam-sign-in) only
</Callout>

<Callout type="info">
  SGI needs a working [OS keyring](https://specifications.freedesktop.org/secret-service/latest/) to securely store your session. This is preconfigured on most desktops, but if sign-in fails, or you get a "your Steam session isn't active anymore" error — see [this troubleshooting entry](/docs/troubleshooting#linux-keyring-secret-service)
</Callout>

<Callout type="warn">
  The `.deb` / `.rpm` versions do not support automatic updates. You'll need to download and install the new package manually for each release
</Callout>

<Steps>
  <Step>
    ### Download [#download-2]

    Download the file matching your distro/format from the [latest release](https://github.com/zevnda/steam-game-idler/releases/latest/) page on GitHub:

    * **Debian/Ubuntu-based**: `Steam.Game.Idler_X.X.X_amd64.deb`
    * **Fedora/openSUSE-based**: `Steam.Game.Idler_X.X.X-1.x86_64.rpm`
    * **Any distro**: `Steam.Game.Idler_X.X.X_amd64.AppImage`
  </Step>

  <Step>
    ### Install [#install-2]

    * **deb**:
      ```bash
      sudo dpkg -i Steam.Game.Idler_X.X.X_amd64.deb
      ```
    * **rpm**:
      ```bash
      sudo rpm -i Steam.Game.Idler_X.X.X-1.x86_64.rpm
      ```
  </Step>

  <Step>
    ### Run [#run-2]

    * **deb/rpm**: launch SGI from your desktop's application launcher
    * **AppImage**: make it executable and run it directly
      ```bash
      chmod +x Steam.Game.Idler_X.X.X_amd64.AppImage
      ./Steam.Game.Idler_X.X.X_amd64.AppImage
      ```
  </Step>
</Steps>

chunks.title: Multi-Account — Multi-Account [#multi-account]
chunks.text:
Multi-Account [#multi-account]


SGI can keep several **Steam Sign-in** accounts signed in and running at the same time, each with its own idling, card farming, and achievement unlocking happening independently. You switch between them from one app window without signing out.

chunks.title: Multi-Account — How Many Accounts Can I Add? [#how-many-accounts-can-i-add]
chunks.text:
How Many Accounts Can I Add? [#how-many-accounts-can-i-add]


The number of **Steam Sign-in** accounts you can have signed in at the same time depends on your [subscription tier](/docs/pro):

|                                   | Free | Casual | Gamer |
| --------------------------------- | :--: | :----: | :---: |
| Concurrent Steam Sign-in accounts |   1  |    3   |   10  |

<Callout type="info">
  You can still have one **Legacy Sign-in** account signed in alongside your **Steam Sign-in** accounts, regardless of tier. It doesn't count against this limit
</Callout>

chunks.title: Multi-Account — Adding an Account [#adding-an-account]
chunks.text:
Adding an Account [#adding-an-account]


<Steps>
  <Step>
    ### Open the account switcher [#open-the-account-switcher]

    Click your account name/avatar at the bottom of the sidebar
  </Step>

  <Step>
    ### Add another account [#add-another-account]

    Click <MockButton type="add-account" />
  </Step>

  <Step>
    ### Sign in [#sign-in]

    Follow the same [Steam Sign-in](/docs/get-started/how-to-sign-in#steam-sign-in) or [Legacy Sign-in](/docs/get-started/how-to-sign-in#legacy-sign-in) steps for the new account
  </Step>
</Steps>

chunks.title: Multi-Account — Switching Between Accounts [#switching-between-accounts]
chunks.text:
Switching Between Accounts [#switching-between-accounts]


Click your account name/avatar at the bottom of the sidebar, then click the account you want to switch to. Every account you've added keeps idling, farming, and unlocking in the background while you're viewing a different one. Switching only changes which account's dashboard you're looking at.

chunks.title: Multi-Account — Signing Out [#signing-out]
chunks.text:
Signing Out [#signing-out]


Click your account name/avatar at the bottom of the sidebar and click <MockButton type="sign-out" /> on the account you no longer want signed in.

chunks.title: Achievement Unlocker — Achievement Unlocker Settings [#achievement-unlocker-settings]
chunks.text:
Achievement Unlocker Settings [#achievement-unlocker-settings]


You'll find these options under <MockButton type="context-cog" content="Settings → Achievement Unlocker" />.

chunks.title: Achievement Unlocker — Idle While Unlocking [#idle-while-unlocking]
chunks.text:
Idle While Unlocking [#idle-while-unlocking]


Keep the game running in the background while achievements are being unlocked

When enabled, SGI will idle the current game during the unlocking process, increasing its playtime alongside the achievements. This makes the activity look more consistent with natural gameplay.

chunks.title: Achievement Unlocker — Run Multiple Games At Once [#run-multiple-games-at-once]
chunks.text:
Run Multiple Games At Once [#run-multiple-games-at-once]


Work through several queued games concurrently instead of one at a time *(Pro Casual tier)*

When enabled, games in the Achievement Unlocker queue are processed concurrently instead of one at a time, each with its own independent unlock schedule. Casual subscribers can run up to 3 games at once; Gamer subscribers can run up to 32, both within the combined limit of 32 games idling at once shared with every other idling feature (see [Playtime Booster](/docs/features/playtime-booster)).

chunks.title: Achievement Unlocker — Skip Hidden Achievements [#skip-hidden-achievements]
chunks.text:
Skip Hidden Achievements [#skip-hidden-achievements]


Skip achievements that the game developer has marked as hidden

Hidden achievements don't reveal their unlock conditions in Steam. Enable this if you prefer to discover and unlock these naturally yourself, while still automating the rest.

chunks.title: Achievement Unlocker — Unlock Interval [#unlock-interval]
chunks.text:
Unlock Interval [#unlock-interval]


Set how long SGI waits between unlocking each achievement *(in minutes)*

You specify a minimum and maximum range. After unlocking an achievement, SGI picks a random wait time within that range before unlocking the next one. This randomization makes the unlock pattern look more natural.

For example, with a range of `60` to `180` minutes, SGI will wait between 1 and 3 hours between each unlock.

* **Minimum value:** 1 minute
* **Maximum value:** 2880 minutes (48 hours)

Per-achievement delays set in the [Custom Order](/docs/features/achievement-unlocker/custom-order-and-unlock-delay) page override this global interval for individual achievements.

chunks.title: Achievement Unlocker — Only Unlock During A Schedule [#only-unlock-during-a-schedule]
chunks.text:
Only Unlock During A Schedule [#only-unlock-during-a-schedule]


Restrict achievement unlocking to a specific time window

When enabled, SGI will only unlock achievements while inside your scheduled time range. Outside of those hours, the Achievement Unlocker continues running but pauses unlocking until the window opens again.

For example, setting a range of `09:00` to `17:00` means SGI will only unlock achievements during business hours and wait overnight without stopping.

chunks.title: Achievement Unlocker — Start Another Task When Done [#start-another-task-when-done]
chunks.text:
Start Another Task When Done [#start-another-task-when-done]


Automatically start another feature once the Achievement Unlocker queue is empty

Enable the checkbox and choose either **Card Farming** or **Auto-Idle** from the dropdown to have it start automatically once every queued game has finished unlocking.

chunks.title: Card Farming — Card Farming Settings [#card-farming-settings]
chunks.text:
Card Farming Settings [#card-farming-settings]


You'll find these options under <MockButton type="context-cog" content="Settings → Card Farming" />.

chunks.title: Card Farming — Hours Until Farmable [#hours-until-farmable]
chunks.text:
Hours Until Farmable [#hours-until-farmable]


How many hours of playtime a game needs before its card drops are considered reachable

See [How It Works](/docs/features/card-farming/how-it-works) for more information on how this setting affects farming behavior.

chunks.title: Card Farming — Farm Multiple Games At Once [#farm-multiple-games-at-once]
chunks.text:
Farm Multiple Games At Once [#farm-multiple-games-at-once]


Farm up to 32 games concurrently instead of one at a time. In some cases this can cause cards to drop significantly slower.

chunks.title: Card Farming — Automatically Farm Cards [#automatically-farm-cards]
chunks.text:
Automatically Farm Cards [#automatically-farm-cards]


Periodically check for owned games with card drops remaining and automatically start farming them *(Pro Gamer tier)*

When enabled, SGI monitors your library on a recurring schedule and starts a farming cycle without you needing to trigger it manually.

chunks.title: Card Farming — Skip Refundable Games *(Steam Sign-in only)* [#skip-refundable-games-steam-sign-in-only]
chunks.text:
Skip Refundable Games *(Steam Sign-in only)* [#skip-refundable-games-steam-sign-in-only]


Don't farm a game while it's still inside Steam's refund window

Skips farming any game bought within the last 14 days that has under 2 hours of playtime, since Steam considers it still eligible for a refund.

chunks.title: Card Farming — Skip Unplayed Games [#skip-unplayed-games]
chunks.text:
Skip Unplayed Games [#skip-unplayed-games]


Skip games that have never been played *(0 playtime)* during card farming

<Callout type="info">
  **Skip Unplayed Games** and **Unplayed Games Only** are mutually exclusive: enabling one will disable the other.
</Callout>

chunks.title: Card Farming — Unplayed Games Only [#unplayed-games-only]
chunks.text:
Unplayed Games Only [#unplayed-games-only]


Only farm cards for games that have never been played *(0 playtime)*

<Callout type="info">
  **Skip Unplayed Games** and **Unplayed Games Only** are mutually exclusive: enabling one will disable the other.
</Callout>

chunks.title: Card Farming — Start Another Task When Done [#start-another-task-when-done]
chunks.text:
Start Another Task When Done [#start-another-task-when-done]


Automatically start another feature once Card Farming finishes

Enable the checkbox and choose either **Achievement Unlocker** or **Auto-Idle** from the dropdown to have it start automatically once your current farming cycle completes.

chunks.title: Customization — Customization Settings [#customization-settings]
chunks.text:
Customization Settings [#customization-settings]


You'll find these options under <MockButton type="context-cog" content="Settings → Customization" />.

chunks.title: Customization — Disable Tooltips [#disable-tooltips]
chunks.text:
Disable Tooltips [#disable-tooltips]


Hide the small informational pop-ups that appear when hovering over elements in the app

Tooltips provide extra context for buttons and settings, but can feel repetitive once you're familiar with the app. Enable this to turn them off.

chunks.title: Customization — Show Recommended Carousel [#show-recommended-carousel]
chunks.text:
Show Recommended Carousel [#show-recommended-carousel]


Show or hide the recommended games carousel on the **Your Games** page

The recommended carousel surfaces games in your library that you haven't played yet. Disable this if you prefer a cleaner view.

chunks.title: Customization — Show Recently Played Carousel [#show-recently-played-carousel]
chunks.text:
Show Recently Played Carousel [#show-recently-played-carousel]


Show or hide the recently played games carousel on the **Your Games** page

The recently played carousel shows the last few games you've run through Steam. Disable this if you don't need quick access to recent games.

chunks.title: Customization — Font [#font]
chunks.text:
Font [#font]


Change the font used throughout the SGI interface *(non-default fonts require Pro Casual tier)*

Every font is bundled with the app, so switching never needs a download. Pro fonts are unlocked with a [Casual or Gamer subscription](/pro).

chunks.title: Customization — Background Image [#background-image]
chunks.text:
Background Image [#background-image]


Set a custom background image for the SGI window *(Pro Casual tier)*

Click <MockButton type="content" content="Choose image" /> to upload any common image file (PNG, JPG, WEBP, etc.) from your computer to use as a background. It's applied as a subtle overlay behind the main UI. Click <MockButton type="clear" /> to remove it and return to the default appearance.

chunks.title: Customization — Theme [#theme]
chunks.text:
Theme [#theme]


Change the color scheme of SGI *(non-default themes require Pro Casual tier)*

| Theme   | Availability      |
| ------- | ----------------- |
| Default | Free              |
| Blue    | Pro (Casual tier) |
| Red     | Pro (Casual tier) |
| Purple  | Pro (Casual tier) |
| Pink    | Pro (Casual tier) |
| Orange  | Pro (Casual tier) |
| Black   | Pro (Casual tier) |
| White   | Pro (Casual tier) |

Click any theme swatch to preview and apply it immediately. Pro themes are unlocked with a [Casual or Gamer subscription](/pro).

chunks.title: Debug — Debug [#debug]
chunks.text:
Debug [#debug]


You'll find these tools under <MockButton type="context-cog" content="Settings → Debug" />. If something isn't working as expected, start here before reporting a bug.

chunks.title: Debug — Logs [#logs]
chunks.text:
Logs [#logs]


The Logs panel displays a live view of SGI's internal activity, including errors and events from features like Card Farming and Achievement Unlocker.

* Click <MockButton type="view-log-file" /> to open today's log file
* Click <MockButton type="clear-logs" /> to clear the log view

<Callout type="info">
  Logs are written to a new file every day, kept in a `logs` folder next to where SGI stores its
  settings and cache: `<install folder>/logs/` for the Windows portable version, or your OS's
  app-data location otherwise (`%appdata%\com.zevnda.steam-game-idler\` on Windows,
  `~/.local/share/com.zevnda.steam-game-idler/` on Linux). <MockButton type="view-log-file" />
  always opens the right one for you, so you don't need to remember the exact path.
</Callout>

If you're reporting a bug on GitHub, include the relevant log files to help diagnose the issue. See the [Troubleshooting](/docs/troubleshooting) guide for more information.

chunks.title: Debug — Reset Settings [#reset-settings]
chunks.text:
Reset Settings [#reset-settings]


<Callout type="warn">
  This action is irreversible
</Callout>

Click <MockButton type="reset-settings" /> to reset all of SGI's settings back to default

This is useful if you've misconfigured something and want to start fresh without wiping everything.

chunks.title: Debug — Clear Data [#clear-data]
chunks.text:
Clear Data [#clear-data]


<Callout type="warn">
  This action is irreversible. You will be signed out of every account in SGI.
</Callout>

Click <MockButton type="clear-data" /> to sign every account out, stop any running automation, and clear all locally-stored app data on this device (settings, feature queues, logs, recent searches, inventory locks, etc).

Use this as a last resort if SGI is behaving unexpectedly and [Reset Settings](/docs/settings/debug#reset-settings) hasn't resolved the issue.

chunks.title: Debug — Export Settings [#export-settings]
chunks.text:
Export Settings [#export-settings]


Click <MockButton type="export-settings" /> to copy your current SGI settings to the clipboard. Use this to:

* Back up your configuration before making changes
* Transfer your settings to another machine
* Attach to a bug report when opening an issue on GitHub

chunks.title: Debug — Open Settings File [#open-settings-file]
chunks.text:
Open Settings File [#open-settings-file]


Click <MockButton type="open-settings-file" /> to open the folder where SGI stores its settings file in File Explorer. Useful for manually inspecting the file, or pasting in an exported settings backup to restore a previous configuration.

chunks.title: Free Games — Free Games Settings [#free-games-settings]
chunks.text:
Free Games Settings [#free-games-settings]


You'll find these options under <MockButton type="context-cog" content="Settings → Free Games" />.

chunks.title: Free Games — Free Game Notifications [#free-game-notifications]
chunks.text:
Free Game Notifications [#free-game-notifications]


Get a system notification when a new free Steam game becomes available

SGI periodically checks for new free games and will notify you when one appears. Note that notifications may not be immediate. There can be a short delay depending on when SGI last checked.

To avoid being notified about games you already own, make sure your games list is up to date by clicking <MockButton type="content" content="Refresh" /> in <MockButton type="your-games" />.

chunks.title: Free Games — Auto Redeem Free Games [#auto-redeem-free-games]
chunks.text:
Auto Redeem Free Games [#auto-redeem-free-games]


Automatically add free Steam games to your account as soon as they become available *(Pro Gamer tier)*

When enabled, SGI will claim free games on your behalf without any input from you. What else this requires depends on how you [signed in](/docs/get-started/how-to-sign-in):

* **Steam Sign-in**: no extra step needed, just turn this on
* **Legacy Sign-in**: you must also click <MockButton type="content" content="Sign in to Steam" /> on this tab first, and stay signed in, for auto-redeem to work

<Callout type="info">
  If you enable Auto Redeem, consider also enabling [Free Game Notifications](#free-game-notifications) so you can see which games were claimed on your behalf.
</Callout>

Also see: [What Counts as a Free Game?](/docs/features/free-games/what-counts-as-a-free-game)

chunks.title: Game Settings — Individual Game Settings [#individual-game-settings]
chunks.text:
Individual Game Settings [#individual-game-settings]


You'll find this page under <MockButton type="context-cog" content="Settings → Game Settings" />. Use it to set per-game limits for playtime, idling, card farming, and achievement unlocking. Select a game from the list, then configure its limits below. Every limit set to `0` means unlimited.

<Callout type="info">
  Enable **Only show games with custom settings** to filter the game list down to just the games you've already customized.
</Callout>

chunks.title: Game Settings — Playtime [#playtime]
chunks.text:
Playtime [#playtime]


These limits apply everywhere a game can be idled: manual [Playtime Booster](/docs/features/playtime-booster), [Auto-Idle](/docs/features/auto-idle), [Achievement Unlocker](/docs/features/achievement-unlocker), and [Card Farming](/docs/features/card-farming) all respect them.

chunks.title: Game Settings — Max Playtime (All Games) [#max-playtime-all-games]
chunks.text:
Max Playtime (All Games) [#max-playtime-all-games]


Automatically stop a game, and remove it from every queue, once its total playtime reaches this many minutes. Applies to every game unless it has its own override below.

chunks.title: Game Settings — Max Playtime [#max-playtime]
chunks.text:
Max Playtime [#max-playtime]


Same as above, but for the selected game only. Overrides **Max Playtime (All Games)** when set.

chunks.title: Game Settings — Idling [#idling]
chunks.text:
Idling [#idling]


These limits only apply to manually and automatically idled games. Card Farming and Achievement Unlocker have their own separate caps below.

chunks.title: Game Settings — Max Idle Time (All Games) [#max-idle-time-all-games]
chunks.text:
Max Idle Time (All Games) [#max-idle-time-all-games]


Set a default maximum idle time (in minutes) that applies to all games. Individual per-game limits take priority over this value when set.

chunks.title: Game Settings — Max Idle Time [#max-idle-time]
chunks.text:
Max Idle Time [#max-idle-time]


Set the maximum idle time (in minutes) for the selected game. SGI will stop idling this game when the time limit is reached, overriding the value above.

chunks.title: Game Settings — Card Farming [#card-farming]
chunks.text:
Card Farming [#card-farming]


These limits only apply to Card Farming sessions.

chunks.title: Game Settings — Max Card Farming Time (All Games) [#max-card-farming-time-all-games]
chunks.text:
Max Card Farming Time (All Games) [#max-card-farming-time-all-games]


Set a default maximum farming time (in minutes) that applies to all games. Individual per-game limits take priority over this value when set.

chunks.title: Game Settings — Max Card Farming Time [#max-card-farming-time]
chunks.text:
Max Card Farming Time [#max-card-farming-time]


Set the maximum farming time (in minutes) for the selected game. SGI will stop farming this game when the time limit is reached, overriding the value above.

chunks.title: Game Settings — Max Card Drops [#max-card-drops]
chunks.text:
Max Card Drops [#max-card-drops]


Set the maximum number of card drops to farm for the selected game before stopping.

Note that because card drop timing is not precisely predictable, SGI will try to stay within this limit but it may not always be exact.

chunks.title: Game Settings — Achievement Unlocker [#achievement-unlocker]
chunks.text: Achievement Unlocker [#achievement-unlocker]

chunks.title: Game Settings — Max Achievement Unlocks [#max-achievement-unlocks]
chunks.text:
Max Achievement Unlocks [#max-achievement-unlocks]


Set the maximum number of achievements to unlock for the selected game. SGI will stop unlocking and remove the game from the Achievement Unlocker queue once this limit is reached.

chunks.title: General — General Settings [#general-settings]
chunks.text:
General Settings [#general-settings]


You'll find these options under <MockButton type="context-cog" content="Settings → General" />.

chunks.title: General — Always Online [#always-online]
chunks.text:
Always Online [#always-online]


Prevents Steam from setting your status as away while SGI is running *(Legacy Sign-in only)*

When enabled, SGI will automatically switch your Steam status back to online if it changes to away, offline, or invisible while the app is running. This is useful when you want to appear active on Steam while games are idling in the background.

Only available for accounts using [Legacy Sign-in](/docs/get-started/how-to-sign-in) (a real local Steam client). **Steam Sign-in** accounts don't need this. See [Online Status](#online-status) below, which covers the same need without any periodic re-checking required.

chunks.title: General — Online Status *(Steam Sign-in only)* [#online-status-steam-sign-in-only]
chunks.text:
Online Status *(Steam Sign-in only)* [#online-status-steam-sign-in-only]


Choose what online status friends see while signed in

Pick which status (Online, Away, Busy, Snooze, Looking to Trade, Looking to Play, Invisible, or Offline) your account shows to friends. Unlike Legacy Sign-in's Always Online above, this status doesn't drift back to Away on its own, so there's nothing to periodically refresh. It's set once and stays that way until you change it.

chunks.title: General — Custom Status While Idling *(Steam Sign-in only · Pro Gamer tier)* [#custom-status-while-idling-steam-sign-in-only--pro-gamer-tier]
chunks.text:
Custom Status While Idling *(Steam Sign-in only · Pro Gamer tier)* [#custom-status-while-idling-steam-sign-in-only--pro-gamer-tier]


Replace the "Playing \[game]" text friends see while idling

Set your own custom message to show instead of the game's name while idling. You can set this before, during, or after idling starts. It only becomes visible to friends once you're actually idling a game you own.

chunks.title: General — Show Games Only *(Steam Sign-in only)* [#show-games-only-steam-sign-in-only]
chunks.text:
Show Games Only *(Steam Sign-in only)* [#show-games-only-steam-sign-in-only]


Hide DLC, soundtracks, videos, and tools from your library

When enabled, only owned games and family-shared games are shown in your library, filtering out non-game items like DLC, soundtracks, videos, and tools. Changing this refreshes your games list.

chunks.title: General — Run At Startup [#run-at-startup]
chunks.text:
Run At Startup [#run-at-startup]


Automatically launch SGI when your computer starts

SGI will be registered to launch at login (Windows startup programs, or your Linux desktop's autostart mechanism) so it runs in the background whenever you log in, without needing to open it manually. Works best when paired with [Start Minimized](#start-minimized).

chunks.title: General — Start Minimized [#start-minimized]
chunks.text:
Start Minimized [#start-minimized]


Launch SGI to the system tray instead of showing the main window

When enabled, SGI opens silently in the background on startup. You can access it at any time by clicking the SGI icon in the system tray. Pairs well with [Run At Startup](#run-at-startup) for a fully hands-off setup.

chunks.title: General — Close to Tray [#close-to-tray]
chunks.text:
Close to Tray [#close-to-tray]


Keep SGI running when you close the window

When enabled, clicking the X button minimizes SGI to the system tray instead of exiting it. To fully close the app, right-click the system tray icon and select `Quit`.

chunks.title: General — Automatically Update Games List [#automatically-update-games-list]
chunks.text:
Automatically Update Games List [#automatically-update-games-list]


Silently refresh your games list in the background so it stays current without a manual refresh *(Pro Casual tier)*

When enabled, SGI periodically checks for changes to your Steam library, such as newly purchased or removed games, and updates the list without requiring a manual refresh. The check runs every 5 minutes by default, or every minute if you've set your own [Steam Web API Key](#steam-web-api-key) below (the shared built-in key checks less often to stay within Steam's rate limits).

chunks.title: General — Language [#language]
chunks.text:
Language [#language]


Choose the display language for SGI

The language is set automatically based on your system settings, but you can change it to any supported language from the dropdown. If you'd like to help translate SGI into your language, see the [contribution guide](https://github.com/zevnda/steam-game-idler/discussions/148).

chunks.title: General — Steam Web API Key [#steam-web-api-key]
chunks.text:
Steam Web API Key [#steam-web-api-key]


Use your own Steam Web API key to access private profile data

By default, SGI fetches your profile and game data from public Steam APIs. Providing your own API key lets SGI access data even when your Steam profile is set to private.

* API keys are free for all Steam accounts. [Get yours here](https://steamcommunity.com/dev/apikey)
* The API key must belong to the same Steam account you're signed into in SGI. If you use multiple accounts, you'll need to set the key for each one separately
* Some features may still be limited with a private profile even with an API key
* Your key is validated against Steam before it's saved, and stored securely rather than in a plain settings file

chunks.title: Inventory Manager — Inventory Manager Settings [#inventory-manager-settings]
chunks.text:
Inventory Manager Settings [#inventory-manager-settings]


You'll find these options under <MockButton type="context-cog" content="Settings → Inventory Manager" />.

<Callout type="info">
  The price you set is what the **buyer pays**. SGI accounts for Steam's 15% transaction fee automatically, so your received amount will be less. See [Marketplace Fees](/docs/features/inventory-manager/marketplace-fees) for details.
</Callout>

chunks.title: Inventory Manager — Currency [#currency]
chunks.text:
Currency [#currency]


Choose the currency used for price display in SGI

This affects prices shown throughout the [Inventory Manager](/docs/features/inventory-manager), including suggested sell prices fetched from the Steam marketplace.

chunks.title: Inventory Manager — Default Price [#default-price]
chunks.text:
Default Price [#default-price]


Choose how SGI determines the default price when listing items

* **Highest Buy Order**: lists at the highest price someone is currently willing to pay for the item. This is more likely to sell quickly
* **Lowest Sell Order**: lists at the lowest price another seller is currently asking. This may take longer to sell but can yield a slightly higher return

This setting only affects the default price applied when using <MockButton type="list-all" />. You can always override the price on individual items.

chunks.title: Inventory Manager — Price Adjustment [#price-adjustment]
chunks.text:
Price Adjustment [#price-adjustment]


Add or subtract a fixed amount from every item's sale price

Useful for undercutting the market or adding a small buffer above the default price. For example, setting `-0.05` reduces every listing price by $0.05.

If the adjusted price falls below your [Sell Limit](#sell-limit) minimum, the item will not be listed.

chunks.title: Inventory Manager — Sell Limit [#sell-limit]
chunks.text:
Sell Limit [#sell-limit]


Set a minimum and maximum price range for listings

Items whose final price falls outside this range will be skipped and not listed for sale. This protects you from accidentally selling valuable items too cheaply or listing common items at unrealistic prices.

For example, with a minimum of `0.05` and a maximum of `2.00`, only items priced between $0.05 and $2.00 will be listed.

chunks.title: Inventory Manager — Sell Delay [#sell-delay]
chunks.text:
Sell Delay [#sell-delay]


Set how long SGI waits between listing each item *(in seconds)*

Steam's marketplace API has strict rate limits. If you list items too quickly, Steam will temporarily block further listings. A higher delay is safer if you're selling a large number of items.

<Callout type="info">
  Manually fetching a price also has a fixed 5-second cooldown between clicks, separate from this setting
</Callout>

chunks.title: Keybinds — Keybinds [#keybinds]
chunks.text:
Keybinds [#keybinds]

chunks.title: Subscription — Subscription Settings [#subscription-settings]
chunks.text:
Subscription Settings [#subscription-settings]


You'll find this tab under <MockButton type="context-cog" content="Settings → Subscription" />

chunks.title: Subscription — Status [#status]
chunks.text:
Status [#status]


Shows whether you're currently subscribed and which tier (**Casual** or **Gamer**), along with your renewal or cancellation date.

* Click <MockButton type="manage-subscription" /> to open your billing portal (Stripe or PayPal, depending on how you subscribed) to update payment details, view invoices, or cancel
* If you're on **Casual**, an <MockButton type="upgrade" /> button also appears next to it to move up to **Gamer**

chunks.title: Subscription — License Key [#license-key]
chunks.text:
License Key [#license-key]


Once you've subscribed, you'll receive a license key by email.

* **Activate**: paste your license key and click <MockButton type="activate" /> to unlock PRO on this device
* **Copy**: click <MockButton type="copy" /> to copy your currently-activated key to the clipboard
* **Clear**: click <MockButton type="clear" /> to remove the key from this device, deactivating PRO here (your subscription itself isn't cancelled, you can re-activate on any device later)

<Callout type="info">

</Callout>

chunks.title: Achievement Manager — How to Manage Steam Achievements Manually [#how-to-manage-steam-achievements-manually]
chunks.text:
How to Manage Steam Achievements Manually [#how-to-manage-steam-achievements-manually]


The Achievement Manager lets you manually unlock and lock achievements for any game in your library, as well as modify game statistics. Unlike the [Achievement Unlocker](/docs/features/achievement-unlocker), this is a one-by-one manual tool: useful for targeting specific achievements without automation.

chunks.title: Achievement Manager — Achievements [#achievements]
chunks.text:
Achievements [#achievements]


<Steps>
  <Step>
    Click <MockButton type="your-games" /> in the sidebar
  </Step>

  <Step>
    Click the <MockButton type="achievement-manager" /> button on individual games to open them in the achievement manager
  </Step>

  <Step>
    On the achievement manager screen you will see a list of achievements for that game, if any are available

    Click <MockButton type="unlock" /> or <MockButton type="lock" /> next to an achievement to unlock or lock it individually

    Click  <MockButton type="unlock-all" /> or <MockButton type="lock-all" /> in the page header to affect every achievement at once

    Use the <MockButton type="checkbox" /> next to each achievement to toggle its state, then click <MockButton type="content" content="Save changes" /> to apply the changes
  </Step>
</Steps>

<Callout type="info">
  Some achievements/statistics are marked **Protected** and can't be modified. See [Special Flags](/docs/features/achievement-manager/special-flags)
</Callout>

chunks.title: Achievement Manager — Statistics [#statistics]
chunks.text:
Statistics [#statistics]


<Steps>
  <Step>
    Click <MockButton type="your-games" /> in the sidebar
  </Step>

  <Step>
    Click the <MockButton type="achievement-manager" /> button on individual games to open them in the achievement manager
  </Step>

  <Step>
    On the achievement manager screen, click the <MockButton type="content" content="Statistics" /> tab in the page header. You will see a list of statistics for that game, if any are available
  </Step>

  <Step>
    Change the `value` of any statistics you want to modify and click <MockButton type="save-changes" />
  </Step>
</Steps>

<DocsCTA />

chunks.title: Special Flags — Special Flags [#special-flags]
chunks.text:
Special Flags [#special-flags]


Some achievements and statistics have restrictions [set by the game's developer](https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/features/achievements#game_server_stats:~:text=Stats%20and%20achievements%20that%20are%20settable%20by%20game%20servers%20cannot%20be%20set%20by%20clients) that affect what you can change. These are indicated directly in the UI.

* **Protected:** Only the game's official servers can modify these. The unlock/lock buttons will be disabled for protected achievements
* **IncrementOnly:** This statistic can only increase in value. You can raise it from 5 to 6, but not lower it from 5 to 4
* **Hidden:** The achievement's description is blurred by default. Hover over it to reveal the text

For statistics, any active flags are shown directly beneath the stat value in the Statistics tab.

chunks.title: Custom Order & Unlock Delay — Custom Order & Unlock Delay [#custom-order--unlock-delay]
chunks.text:
Custom Order & Unlock Delay [#custom-order--unlock-delay]


The Custom Order & Unlock Delay feature lets you set the exact order in which achievements are unlocked, and allows you to skip any that you don't want unlocked.

The `unlock delay` is how long SGI waits after unlocking one achievement before unlocking the next. For example, if you set a delay of 10 minutes on achievement one, SGI will unlock achievement one, wait 10 minutes, and then unlock achievement two.

Per-achievement unlock delays override the global value set in [<MockButton type="context-cog" content="Settings → Achievement Unlocker → Unlock Interval" />](/docs/settings/achievement-unlocker#unlock-interval). If no per-achievement unlock delay is set, the [Unlock Interval](/docs/settings/achievement-unlocker#unlock-interval) value is used.

You can customize the order, set delays, or both. Each step is optional.

<Steps>
  <Step>
    Follow steps 1 and 2 from the [Default Mode](/docs/features/achievement-unlocker#default-mode) section
  </Step>

  <Step>
    Switch to the <MockButton type="content" content="Queue" /> tab
  </Step>

  <Step>
    Click <MockButton type="unlock-order" /> below the game you want to customize
  </Step>

  <Step>
    Drag and drop achievements by grabbing the <MockButton type="grabber" /> to set their unlock order
  </Step>

  <Step>
    Click <MockButton type="checkbox" /> to deselect achievements and skip them from being unlocked
  </Step>

  <Step>
    Enter a value (in minutes) in **Delay before first unlock** to set how long SGI waits before unlocking the very first achievement
  </Step>

  <Step>
    Enter a delay (in minutes) in the input field of each achievement to set how long SGI waits after unlocking that achievement before unlocking the next one
  </Step>

  <Step>
    Click <MockButton type="save-alt" /> and then click <MockButton type="achievement-unlocker-action" />
  </Step>
</Steps>

chunks.title: Import Timings — Import Timings [#import-timings]
chunks.text:
Import Timings [#import-timings]


The Import Timings feature lets you copy the unlock order and achievement delays from another Steam user's profile. This is useful for matching a specific playstyle or replicating naturally-timed unlocks.

<Callout type="info">
  The target profile and their game details must be set to public on Steam. You can verify this by viewing their games list in an incognito browser window.
</Callout>

<Steps>
  <Step>
    Follow steps 1 and 2 from the [Default Mode](/docs/features/achievement-unlocker#default-mode) section
  </Step>

  <Step>
    Switch to the <MockButton type="content" content="Queue" /> tab
  </Step>

  <Step>
    Click <MockButton type="unlock-order" /> below the game you want to customize
  </Step>

  <Step>
    Click <MockButton type="import-timings" /> in the top-right of the custom order page
  </Step>

  <Step>
    Enter the target user's **SteamID64**, **profile URL**, or **username** and click <MockButton type="content" content="Import" />

    * To find users with legitimate achievements, try achievement tracking sites like [Steam Hunters](https://steamhunters.com/), search for the game, open the **Players** tab, and copy a username from there
  </Step>

  <Step>
    The achievement list will be reordered to match their unlock sequence, with delays calculated from the time between each unlock. Any achievement not unlocked by the target profile will be skipped. You can still adjust the order and delays manually before saving
  </Step>

  <Step>
    Click <MockButton type="save-alt" /> and then click <MockButton type="achievement-unlocker-action" />
  </Step>
</Steps>

chunks.title: Achievement Unlocker — How to Unlock Steam Achievements Automatically [#how-to-unlock-steam-achievements-automatically]
chunks.text:
How to Unlock Steam Achievements Automatically [#how-to-unlock-steam-achievements-automatically]


The Achievement Unlocker automatically unlocks achievements for your Steam games over time, with customizable delays and ordering to mimic natural gameplay.

<Callout type="info">
  Configure this feature's settings in [Settings → Achievement Unlocker](/docs/settings/achievement-unlocker) before using it
</Callout>

chunks.title: Achievement Unlocker — Default Mode [#default-mode]
chunks.text:
Default Mode [#default-mode]


In default mode, achievements are unlocked in order of global achievement rarity (most common first), with the delay set in [<MockButton type="context-cog" content="Settings → Achievement Unlocker → Unlock Interval" />](/docs/settings/achievement-unlocker#unlock-interval).

If you want to define a custom order, and dial in more accurate delays, use the [Custom Order & Unlock Delay](/docs/features/achievement-unlocker/custom-order-and-unlock-delay)

<Steps>
  <Step>
    Click <MockButton type="achievement-unlocker" /> in the sidebar
  </Step>

  <Step>
    Go to the <MockButton type="all-games" /> tab and click the <MockButton type="context-add" /> button on individual games to add them to your queue
  </Step>

  <Step>
    Optionally, you can customize the unlock order and set delays for individual achievements by [following these steps](/docs/features/achievement-unlocker/custom-order-and-unlock-delay)
  </Step>

  <Step>
    Switch to the <MockButton type="content" content="Queue" /> tab to review what you've added, then click <MockButton type="achievement-unlocker-action" />
  </Step>
</Steps>

While running, each active game shows a live countdown to its next achievement, with the next several upcoming achievements listed below it.

<DocsCTA />

chunks.title: Blacklisting Games — Blacklisting Games [#blacklisting-games]
chunks.text:
Blacklisting Games [#blacklisting-games]


You can blacklist specific games from being farmed for cards by going to the <MockButton type="content" content="Games With Drops" /> tab and clicking the <MockButton type="blacklist" /> button on individual games.

Blacklisted games will not be farmed for cards, even if they have card drops remaining. A blacklisted game is automatically removed from your whitelist.

To view or un-blacklist games, switch to the <MockButton type="content" content="Blacklisted" /> tab.

chunks.title: Card Drop Times — Reasons Cards May Not Be Dropping [#reasons-cards-may-not-be-dropping]
chunks.text:
Reasons Cards May Not Be Dropping [#reasons-cards-may-not-be-dropping]


New Steam accounts and accounts that have recently refunded a game fall under the [Limited User Account](https://help.steampowered.com/en/faqs/view/71D3-35C2-AD96-AA3A) restrictions and may have to spend a minimum of **$5.00 USD**, and/or wait three hours before the first card will drop.

If your account isn't Limited and cards still aren't dropping, one of the following is usually the cause:

* **No card drops remaining** — each game only awards half a card set (rounded up) per license, plus extra drops for in-game spending on free-to-play titles. Check the game's remaining drop count on its [badge page](https://steamcommunity.com/my/badges).
* **Offline mode** — Steam can't register playtime or issue drops for a game while your account is not connected to the Steam servers (e.g. no internet connection). This is not the same as setting your account status to "Offline", which has no affect on whether cards will drop or not.
* **Not enough playtime yet** — most games (especially those purchased within the last 14 days) need around 2-3 hours of accumulated playtime before the first card drops, separate from the Limited Account delay above. This is to prevent users from buying games, farming them for cards, and then refunding the game before the 2-hour playtime refund limit is reached. This is only true for some users and not all.
* **Newly added Steam store games** — games that are newly added to the Steam store can take until Steam's next weekly maintenance (Wednesdays, Pacific time) to register, and drops may not count until then.
* **Different per-game intervals** — each game's developer can set their own [card drop interval](https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/features/inventory/schema#PlaytimeDrops). Most games drop a card every 30 minutes, while others can take up to 2 hours
* **An unstable internet connection** while idling can prevent a completed drop timer from being tracked correctly.
* **The game is [marked as private](https://help.steampowered.com/en/faqs/view/1150-C06F-4D62-4966)** on your Steam profile.
* **The game was obtained through Family Sharing** — only the license owner's account receives card drops.
* **The game is in your [Card Farming blacklist](/docs/features/card-farming/blacklisting-games)**.

chunks.title: How It Works — How Card Farming Works [#how-card-farming-works]
chunks.text:
How Card Farming Works [#how-card-farming-works]


Card Farming runs in two phases, switching between them automatically as needed:

1. **Building playtime** — not every account needs this
   * Some Steam accounts may have restrictions on getting card drops until a game passes a certain amount of playtime, while others can drop cards immediately with no wait at all. Account restrictions usually aren't permanent and it can change over time (e.g. refunding a game can turn a previously unrestricted account into a restricted one — see below).
   * Games that haven't cleared this threshold yet are idled in batches of up to 32 first to get the necessary playtime needed to start dropping cards.
   * You can, and should test this yourself by following the [How To Check If Your Account Is Restricted](#how-to-check-if-your-account-is-restricted) steps below to see if your account is restricted or not. If you've confirmed your account isn't restricted, go to <MockButton type="context-cog" content="Settings → Card Farming" /> and set [Hours until farmable](/docs/settings/card-farming#hours-until-farmable) to `0` to skip this phase entirely.
2. **Farming** — once a game has enough playtime, Card Farming switches to farming it on its own until all of its remaining cards have dropped, then moves on to the next game that's ready. If no games are ready, it will go back to the first phase and continue building playtime until a game is ready to farm again.

During both phases, Card Farming will periodically start and stop games to ensure that Steam registers playtime correctly, and can even help promote card drops. It is recommended you set your Steam status to "Offline" or "Invisible" to prevent spamming your friends with status updates. You may also see `SteamUtility` processes starting and stopping in your desktop's task manager, this is normal and expected behavior.

chunks.title: How It Works — How To Check If Your Account Is Restricted [#how-to-check-if-your-account-is-restricted]
chunks.text:
How To Check If Your Account Is Restricted [#how-to-check-if-your-account-is-restricted]


Since there's no way to look this up directly, the only reliable way to know for sure is a short test

<Callout type="info">
  This isn't a one-time answer. Restriction status can change (requesting a refund is a common trigger), so it's worth repeating this test occasionally rather than assuming your first result holds forever.
</Callout>

<Steps>
  <Step>
    Pick 3-5 games you own that have card drops remaining and **zero recorded playtime**. Go to the <MockButton type="content" content="Games With Drops" /> tab and click the <MockButton type="context-add" /> button on each of those games to add them to your whitelist
  </Step>

  <Step>
    Go to <MockButton type="context-cog" content="Settings → Card Farming" /> and temporarily set [Hours until farmable](/docs/settings/card-farming#hours-until-farmable) to `0`

    Also make sure [Farm multiple games at once](/docs/settings/card-farming#farm-multiple-games-at-once) is **disabled** so that only one game is farmed at a time
  </Step>

  <Step>
    Click <MockButton type="card-farming" /> in the sidebar, then click <MockButton type="card-farming-action" /> to start farming those games
  </Step>

  <Step>
    Monitor the progress of each game for roughly 30-60 minutes

    * If **any** of them dropped a card within roughly the first 30-60 minutes, your account isn't restricted, and you can leave **Hours Until Farmable** at `0`
    * If **none** of them dropped anything for several hours, your account is likely restricted. Note roughly how long the first drop took and set **Hours Until Farmable** to match — `3` is a reasonable starting point if you'd rather skip testing altogether
  </Step>
</Steps>

chunks.title: Card Farming — How to Farm Steam Trading Cards Automatically [#how-to-farm-steam-trading-cards-automatically]
chunks.text:
How to Farm Steam Trading Cards Automatically [#how-to-farm-steam-trading-cards-automatically]

<Callout type="warn">

</Callout>

How to Claim Free Steam Games Automatically [#how-to-claim-free-steam-games-automatically]


The Free Games feature allows you to discover and claim free games on Steam, either manually or automatically. This is perfect for users who want to expand their game library without spending money.

<Callout type="info">
  DLC, free-to-play games, and games that you already own are not shown in the Free Games list
</Callout>

chunks.title: Free Games — Manual Redemption [#manual-redemption]
chunks.text:
Manual Redemption [#manual-redemption]


<Steps>
  <Step>
    Click <MockButton type="free-games" /> in the sidebar
  </Step>

  <Step>
    Click the <MockButton type="content" content="Claim" /> button on individual games to claim them
  </Step>

  <Step>
    A Steam store login window will open, sign in to your Steam account in the new window via:

    * Username and password
    * Scanning the QR Code

    Optionally, if you would prefer to not sign into your Steam account, you can visit the game's Steam store page in your browser and claim it manually.
  </Step>

  <Step>
    After claiming a free game, refresh your games list by clicking <MockButton type="content" content="Refresh" /> in the page header of <MockButton type="your-games" />
  </Step>

Automated Redemption [#automated-redemption]


How you enable this depends on how you [signed in](/docs/get-started/how-to-sign-in)

  </Step>

Notifications [#notifications]

chunks.title: What Counts as a Free Game — What Counts as a Free Game [#what-counts-as-a-free-game]
chunks.text:
What Counts as a Free Game [#what-counts-as-a-free-game]


SGI only considers a game to be free if it is temporarily available for `$0.00` as part of a promotion or sale on the Steam store.

This is different to free-to-play games, which have no price and are always available for free. Free-to-play games are not shown in the Free Games list.

chunks.title: Inventory Manager — How to Manage and Sell Steam Inventory Items Automatically [#how-to-manage-and-sell-steam-inventory-items-automatically]
chunks.text:
How to Manage and Sell Steam Inventory Items Automatically [#how-to-manage-and-sell-steam-inventory-items-automatically]


The Inventory Manager feature allows you to manage your Steam inventory directly within SGI, including the ability to view all your marketable items (trading cards, foil cards, emoticons, backgrounds, and more) and sell them on the Steam marketplace.

<Callout type="warn">
  This feature uses an undocumented Steam API endpoint with strict rate limits to fetch card prices. If you encounter errors while selling cards or fetching card prices, please try increasing the [Sell Delay](/docs/settings/inventory-manager#sell-delay), or wait a few hours before trying  again
</Callout>

<Callout type="info">
  You must add your [Steam Credentials](/docs/steam-credentials) before you can use this feature.

  Users using [Steam Sign-in](/docs/get-started/how-to-sign-in) with a [Gamer tier subscription](/pro) do not need to manually enter their Steam credentials.
</Callout>

<Callout type="info">
  Configure this feature's settings in [Settings → Inventory Manager](/docs/settings/inventory-manager) before using it
</Callout>

<Steps>
  <Step>
    Click <MockButton type="inventory-manager" /> in the sidebar
  </Step>

  #### Sell individual items [#sell-individual-items]

  <Steps>
    <Step>
      Find the item you want to sell and input a sale price
    </Step>

    <Step>
      Click the <MockButton type="list-card" /> button to list the item
    </Step>
  </Steps>

  #### Sell multiple selected items [#sell-multiple-selected-items]

  <Steps>
    <Step>
      Find the items you want to sell and input a sale price for each one
    </Step>

    <Step>
      Click <MockButton type="list-selected" /> to list the selected items
    </Step>
  </Steps>

  #### Sell all items [#sell-all-items]

  <Steps>
    <Step>
      Click <MockButton type="list-all" /> to list all items in your inventory
    </Step>
  </Steps>

  #### Sell duplicate items [#sell-duplicate-items]

  <Steps>
    <Step>
      Click <MockButton type="sell-dupes" /> to automatically list all duplicate items for sale, keeping one copy of each
    </Step>
  </Steps>

  <Step>
    Confirm each listing via the Steam mobile app, the [Steam market page](https://steamcommunity.com/market/), or via email depending on your [Steam Guard](https://help.steampowered.com/en/faqs/view/06B0-26E6-2CF8-254C) settings
  </Step>

  <Step>
    Click <MockButton type="refresh" /> in the page header to update your card list
  </Step>
</Steps>

Removing Listings [#removing-listings]

chunks.title: Marketplace Fees — Marketplace Fees [#marketplace-fees]
chunks.text:
Marketplace Fees [#marketplace-fees]


Steam charges a [15% transaction fee](https://help.steampowered.com/en/faqs/view/61F0-72B7-9A18-C70B#steamfee) on each marketplace sale, which is made up of two parts:

* **Steam Transaction Fee (5%)**: This goes to Valve for facilitating the transaction.
* **Game Publisher Fee (10%)**: This goes to the publisher of the game the item is from (not just Valve games; all publishers receive this fee for their own items).

SGI automatically accounts for the 15% Steam transaction fee when you set a sale price. The price you enter is what the **buyer pays**. SGI works out the correct listing price so that the buyer pays exactly that amount.

> If you set a price of `$0.50`, the buyer pays `$0.50` and you receive `$0.44` after fees.

chunks.title: Pricing Details — Pricing Details [#pricing-details]
chunks.text:
Pricing Details [#pricing-details]


When you use <MockButton type="list-all" />, the price used depends on your [Default Sell Option](/docs/settings/inventory-manager#default-sell-option) setting:

* **Highest Buy Order**: lists each item at its `highest_buy_order`. If that price isn't available, it falls back to the `lowest_sell_order`. If neither price is available, the item won't be listed.
* **Lowest Sell Order**: lists each item at its `lowest_sell_order`. If that price isn't available, the item won't be listed.

chunks.title: Account Switcher — Account Switcher
chunks.text:
Account Switcher


This is source content for the AI Assistant's knowledge base (see `scripts/build-ai-corpus.mjs`),
generated by reading the actual `src/features/account-switcher/` component code so the AI
Assistant can describe exactly what a user sees and clicks, not just what the feature does.

UI changes in a way that would make the description below inaccurate.

chunks.title: Account Switcher — Opening the switcher
chunks.text:
Opening the switcher


The account switcher lives at the bottom of the sidebar as a row showing the active account's
avatar, its display name, and a small down-chevron on the right. Clicking it opens a popover above
it listing every signed-in account. When the sidebar is collapsed to its compact icon rail, this
row shrinks to just the avatar (hovering it shows the account name in a tooltip) — the popover
contents are identical either way.

chunks.title: Account Switcher — Reading an account row
chunks.text:
Reading an account row


Each row in the popover shows an avatar, the account's persona name (or its username/Steam ID if
that hasn't resolved yet), and a small label underneath reading either "Signed in with Steam"
(agent-mode accounts) or "Local Steam client" (CLI-mode accounts). A small solid dot on the
avatar's bottom-right corner appears while that account has live automation running (idling, card
farming, or achievement unlocking). The currently active account's row has a soft highlighted
background.

A row can also show one of two other badges next to the mode label:

- A "GAMER" tier badge — this account is signed in but currently over your subscription's
  concurrent-account limit (e.g. after a downgrade). The row stays clickable, just dimmed; clicking
  it opens the upgrade screen instead of switching to it. It is never signed out automatically.
- A red "Signed in elsewhere" badge with a small triangle-exclamation icon — this account's session
  was taken over by a sign-in on another device or session, so its automation has been paused.
  Hovering the badge shows a tooltip explaining this. Clicking the row opens the "Signed in on
  another device" reconnect dialog instead of switching to it (see below).

Each row also has a sign-out icon (a door-with-arrow icon) on its far right. Clicking it signs that
account out — if it has no automation running, it signs out immediately; if it does, a confirmation
dialog titled "Sign out?" appears first, warning that this will stop the automation currently
running for that account.

chunks.title: Account Switcher — Switching accounts
chunks.text:
Switching accounts


Clicking anywhere on a row (other than its sign-out button) switches to that account, unless it's
over-cap or flagged for reauth (see above), in which case the click reroutes to the upgrade or
reconnect flow instead. While a switch is in progress the row's sign-out icon is replaced by a
small spinner. Switching always navigates you to the main games page and shows a toast confirming
"Switched to <name>". If the target is a local (CLI-mode) account and Steam isn't currently running,
switching is blocked with a warning toast and the app's Steam-required warning dialog appears
instead.

chunks.title: Account Switcher — Adding another account
chunks.text:
Adding another account


At the bottom of the popover, below a thin divider, is an "Add another account" row with a plus
icon. Clicking it opens the "Add account" modal, which reuses the same sign-in building blocks as
the main sign-in screen: a landing step to choose Steam Sign-in (agent mode, via QR code or
username/password) or Legacy Sign-in (local Steam client mode), followed by that method's normal
credential/QR/guard-code/account-picker screens. A successful sign-in closes the modal, navigates
to the games page, and shows a toast reading "Added <name>".

Two things can restrict this screen:
- If you already have a local (CLI-mode) account signed in, the Legacy Sign-in option is disabled —
  only one local account can ever be active at a time.
- If you've reached your subscription tier's limit on concurrent Steam Sign-in accounts, the Steam
  Sign-in option shows the limit reached ("The [tier] plan allows N accounts signed in with Steam at
  a time. Sign out of one to add another, or upgrade for more.") and, for Casual/Free tiers, stays
  clickable with a tier badge that opens the upgrade screen instead of a sign-in form. Gamer-tier
  accounts that hit their own maximum see a plain disabled button instead, since there's no higher
  tier left to upsell.

chunks.title: Account Switcher — Reconnecting a "signed in elsewhere" account
chunks.text:
Reconnecting a "signed in elsewhere" account


Clicking a row flagged "Signed in elsewhere" (or its badge) opens the "Signed in on another device"
modal. It explains that the account was signed in elsewhere so its automation was paused, and that
Steam Sign-in only allows one active session per account — if you'd like to keep playing games
while Steam Game Idler runs at the same time, it suggests using Legacy Sign-in instead. It offers
two buttons:

- "Reconnect" — attempts to resume that same account's session using its saved sign-in, taking the
  session back from whichever device currently holds it. Shows a spinner while in progress, and an
  inline error banner if it fails.
- "Use a different sign-in method" — closes this dialog and opens the same "Add another account"
  modal described above, letting you sign that account in a different way (for example switching it
  to Legacy Sign-in).

The badge and dialog clear on their own once a reconnect actually succeeds; there's nothing to
manually dismiss.

chunks.title: Achievement Manager — Achievement Manager
chunks.text:
Achievement Manager


This is source content for the AI Assistant's knowledge base (see `scripts/build-ai-corpus.mjs`),
generated by reading the actual `src/features/achievement-manager/` component code so the AI
Assistant can describe exactly what a user sees and clicks, not just what the feature does.
Regenerate this file (via the `/generate-ui-guide achievement-manager` skill) whenever this
feature's UI changes in a way that would make the description below inaccurate.

Achievement Manager is the single-game overlay for viewing and editing one game's achievements and
statistics directly (as opposed to the Achievement Unlocker, which automates unlocking across a
queue of games). It opens as a full-screen modal over whichever page you were on, with the game's
own hero/background art faded in behind everything.

chunks.title: Achievement Manager — Opening the overlay and its header
chunks.text:
Opening the overlay and its header


The overlay's header has a back/close button (an X) on the top-left, the game's name next to it, and
two small icon buttons: a Steam icon ("View on Steam") that opens that game's Steam Community
achievement page in your browser, and a SteamDB icon ("View on SteamDB") that opens its SteamDB
stats page. Next to those sit two tabs, "Achievements" and "Statistics". On the right side of the
header is a search box that filters whichever tab is currently active by name. If the game has any
"protected" achievements or statistics, a warning banner appears below the header row: "Some items
are protected — Achievements or statistics marked as protected are set by the game's server and
can't be changed by clients."

chunks.title: Achievement Manager — Viewing and toggling achievements
chunks.text:
Viewing and toggling achievements


The Achievements tab shows a trophy icon with an "X / Y unlocked" readout and a small progress bar
next to it (both turn gold once every unlockable achievement is unlocked). Below that is a toolbar
with a sort dropdown, an "Unlock all" button, a "Lock all" button (red), and a circular refresh
button.

Each achievement is its own card row containing, left to right: a checkbox, the achievement's icon
(a small badge in the icon's bottom-right corner shows a green checkmark if unlocked or a grey lock
if not), the achievement's name with a rarity badge next to it when global unlock-rate data is
available (a percentage plus a tier word — Common, Uncommon, Rare, Epic, or Legendary, each in its
own color), its description underneath, and on the far right either an "Unlock"/"Lock" button (a
padlock icon, green to unlock or red to lock) or, for a protected achievement, a disabled ban-icon
button with a tooltip explaining it's set by the game server and can't be changed by clients.
Hidden achievements that aren't yet unlocked have their description blurred until you hover over it.

The checkbox on each row is a staging control, not an immediate action: an already-unlocked
achievement's checkbox starts checked, and unchecking it stages that achievement to be locked; a
locked achievement's checkbox starts unchecked, and checking it stages it to be unlocked. Protected
achievements have their checkbox disabled entirely. Once at least one achievement is staged, an
"Apply changes (N)" button appears in the toolbar — pressing it (after confirming in a dialog) locks
and/or unlocks every staged achievement in one pass and clears the staged set. Pressing an
individual row's own Unlock/Lock button instead applies that one achievement immediately and clears
it from any staged set.

"Unlock all" and "Lock all" each open a confirmation dialog ("Unlock all achievements?" / "Lock all
achievements?") before acting on every unprotected achievement in the game — they're disabled when
there's nothing left to unlock or lock, respectively.

chunks.title: Achievement Manager — Viewing and editing statistics
chunks.text:
Viewing and editing statistics


The Statistics tab shows a count of the game's statistics and, once you've changed any, an "N
edited" pill next to it. The toolbar has a "Save changes" button (disabled until something's
edited, and labeled "Save changes (N)" once something is), a red "Reset all" button, and a refresh
button.

Each statistic is a card row: an icon (a small trending-up badge appears in its corner, with a
tooltip reading "This statistic can only increase, never decrease," for increment-only stats), the
stat's name with its raw flags text underneath, and a numeric stepper input on the right for editing
its value directly. A stat you've changed gets an "Edited" pill next to its name and a highlighted
border. A protected statistic shows its current value in a plain read-only pill with a ban icon
instead of an editable input.

Editing values doesn't save anything by itself — nothing is written until you press "Save changes,"
which applies every edited value in one pass and clears the edited set on success. "Reset all" asks
for confirmation ("Reset all statistics? — This will reset every statistic for this game back to
its default value. This can't be undone.") before resetting every statistic to its default.

Achievement Unlocker

generated by reading the actual `src/features/achievement-unlocker/` component code so the AI
Assistant can describe exactly what a user sees and clicks, not just what the feature does.

feature's UI changes in a way that would make the description below inaccurate.

chunks.title: Achievement Unlocker — Adding games to the queue
chunks.text:
Adding games to the queue


Open the Achievement Unlocker page from the sidebar. It has a "Browse" tab (pick games from your
library to add) and a "Queue" tab (games waiting to be unlocked, shown as a grid of game cards with
their cover art). Adding a game from Browse puts it into the Queue.

chunks.title: Achievement Unlocker — Reordering achievements and choosing unlock order
chunks.text:
Reordering achievements and choosing unlock order


Each game card in the Queue tab has two small icon buttons in its top-right corner: an "Edit unlock
order" button (a sort/arrows icon) and a remove button (an X icon). Clicking the sort icon opens a
full-screen order editor for that specific game.

Inside the order editor, each achievement appears as its own row containing, from left to right:

- A checkbox — unchecking it skips that achievement (it stays in the list, greyed out with a
  "Skipped" label, but won't be unlocked).
- The achievement's icon image.
- The achievement's name, its description below it, and (if available) a small rarity percentage
  badge showing how many other Steam players have it.
- A grabber icon on the far right — six dots arranged in two rows. Click and hold this handle to
  drag the achievement up or down in the list. The order you drop it in is the exact order Steam
  Game Idler will unlock that game's achievements in.

At the top of the list there's also a delay control for how long to wait before the very first
achievement unlocks, and each row's connecting space between achievements lets you set a delay
before that specific achievement unlocks relative to the one before it — this is what makes unlocks
land with natural-feeling gaps instead of firing all at once.

The order editor's header (top of the screen) has a close button (X, top-left) and the game's name.
On the top-right: a "Reset" button (red) that clears any custom order/skip/delay changes back to
default, and an "Import" button that pulls the exact achievement order and delay timings from any
public Steam profile that already has them (Gamer-tier subscribers only — Casual and Free-tier
accounts see this button with a small tier badge instead, which opens the upgrade screen).

Changes made in the order editor are saved via a "Save" button at the bottom of the screen once
you're done arranging things — nothing is applied until you save.

chunks.title: Agent (Steam Sign-in) Sign-in Screen — Agent (Steam Sign-in) Sign-in Screen
chunks.text:
Agent (Steam Sign-in) Sign-in Screen


This is source content for the AI Assistant's knowledge base (see `scripts/build-ai-corpus.mjs`),
generated by reading the actual `src/features/agent-sign-in/` component code so the AI Assistant
can describe exactly what a user sees and clicks, not just what the feature does. Regenerate this
file (via the `/generate-ui-guide agent-sign-in` skill) whenever this feature's UI changes in a way
that would make the description below inaccurate.

This is the screen shown after choosing "Steam Sign-in" on the sign-in landing page (or from "Add
another account" in the account switcher). It signs a Steam account in without needing a local
Steam client running.

chunks.title: Agent (Steam Sign-in) Sign-in Screen — The combined credentials + QR layout
chunks.text:
The combined credentials + QR layout


The screen shows two sign-in methods side by side in one card, separated by a vertical divider, and
both are live at the same time — completing either one signs you in, and completing one
automatically cancels the other:

- Left column, labeled "Sign in with account name": a username field, a password field, and a
  "Sign in" button. An incorrect attempt shows a "Couldn't sign in" alert above the fields with a
  reason ("Incorrect username or password.", a denial message, or a generic retry message).
- Right column, labeled "Or sign in with QR": a QR code (rendered as a real scannable code, not a
  placeholder image) with the instruction "Use the Steam Mobile app to sign in via QR code."
  underneath. If the QR challenge itself fails to load, this column shows an error message and a
  "Try again" button instead.

A back button (top-left, an arrow) returns to the sign-in method choice — but only while you're
still on the form itself; once you're into a Steam Guard code step, the guard code screen's own
"Cancel" button is the way back instead, since backing out silently at that point wouldn't clean up
the in-flight sign-in attempt.

chunks.title: Agent (Steam Sign-in) Sign-in Screen — Entering a Steam Guard code
chunks.text:
Entering a Steam Guard code


If Steam requires additional verification after submitting credentials, the screen switches to a
dedicated Steam Guard step (this replaces the whole two-column layout, not just one side):

- **Mobile authenticator code**: titled "Check your Steam Mobile app", asking you to "Enter the
  code from the Steam Mobile app."
- **Email code**: titled "Check your email", showing "We sent a code to <email>. Enter it below."
- **Confirmation-only**: titled "Confirm this sign-in", showing just a spinner and asking you to
  approve the request in the Steam Mobile app — there's no code to type here, only a "Cancel"
  button while you wait.

For the two code-entry variants, the code field is a 5-character one-time-code input (one box per
character). Entering an incorrect code shows "That code wasn't correct. Please try again." above
the input and marks it invalid. The "Verify" button stays disabled until all 5 characters are
entered, and shows a loading state while submitting. A "Cancel" button below it aborts the sign-in
attempt entirely and returns you to the form.

chunks.title: Agent (Steam Sign-in) Sign-in Screen — What happens on success
chunks.text:
What happens on success


A successful sign-in (from either the credentials form or the QR code) shows a full-screen spinner
briefly, then navigates straight to the dashboard's games page — there's no separate "success"
screen to click through.

chunks.title: Auto Idle — Auto Idle
chunks.text:
Auto Idle


This is source content for the AI Assistant's knowledge base (see `scripts/build-ai-corpus.mjs`),

chunks.text:
Page layout and header


The header shows the page title, a "N games queued" (or "No games queued") subtitle, a "Start"
button (a filled play-triangle icon), and a plus-icon button that opens the "Add game manually"
dialog (add a game by its Steam App ID when it doesn't show up automatically — has a Name field and

least one queued game is enabled, and immediately begins idling every currently enabled game in the
queue.

Below the header are two tabs: "All Games" and "Queue".

chunks.title: Auto Idle — Adding games from All Games
chunks.text:
Adding games from All Games


The "All Games" tab is a grid of your owned games (with a sort dropdown above it) — each card shows
the game's thumbnail, its name, and a small icon-only button in the corner: a plus icon if it isn't
queued yet, or a checkmark if it already is. Clicking it toggles that game in or out of the queue.

chunks.title: Auto Idle — Managing the queue
chunks.text:
Managing the queue


The "Queue" tab shows the games you've added as a grid of draggable cards. Each card has the game's
thumbnail and name, a toggle switch, and a remove button (an X icon). The switch controls whether
that game is actually included the next time idling starts — a game can stay in the queue without
being started, and a disabled card renders dimmed. Removing a card takes it out of the queue
entirely.

Cards can be dragged (click and hold, then drag) to reorder the queue — dropping updates the
persisted order immediately. While in the Queue tab (and it has at least one game), a "Clear"
button appears next to the tabs; clicking it opens a confirmation dialog ("Clear the automatic
idler queue? — This will remove all N games from the automatic idler queue.") before wiping the
entire queue.
