chunks.title: Card Farming — Connecting before you can farm
chunks.text:
Connecting before you can farm


The first time you open Card Farming (or whenever your Steam Community session needs
re-establishing), the page shows a connect panel instead of any game list. It offers an
"Automatic" tab ("Signs in to Steam Community automatically to check for drops.") and a "Manual"
tab for pasting your own Steam cookies — the manual option works on every tier, while the
automatic one requires a Gamer subscription. A "Learn more" link and a note about previously saved
credentials also appear here. Connecting only proves your session works and loads the games list —
it doesn't start farming by itself.

chunks.title: Card Farming — Starting and stopping
chunks.text:
Starting and stopping


Once connected, the header shows "Not farming" or "Farming N games", a "Start" button (a filled
play icon, disabled if there are no eligible games with drops), a settings (gear) icon that opens
Card Farming's tab in the Settings modal, and — once running — the Start button is replaced by a
red "Stop farming" button.

chunks.title: Card Farming — Browsing games with drops
chunks.text:
Browsing games with drops


The "Games With Drops" tab lists every owned game that still has card drops remaining, as a grid of
cards showing the game's thumbnail, name, and a "N drops remaining" count. Each card has two
icon-only buttons: a ban icon that blacklists the game (removing it from this list permanently
until un-blacklisted from the Blacklisted tab) and a plus/checkmark icon that adds or removes it
from your whitelist.

chunks.title: Card Farming — Using the whitelist and blacklist tabs
chunks.text:
Using the whitelist and blacklist tabs


The "Whitelisted" tab shows games you've explicitly restricted farming to — if this list is empty,
farming considers every owned game with drops; adding at least one game here narrows it to just
those. Each card has a remove (X) button. When non-empty, a "Clear" button next to the tabs opens a
confirmation dialog before wiping the whole whitelist ("This will remove all N games from the card
farming whitelist. Farming will go back to considering every owned game with drops.").

The "Blacklisted" tab shows games you've excluded from ever being farmed, each with its own remove
button to un-blacklist it, and the same kind of "Clear" confirmation for wiping the entire
blacklist.

chunks.title: Card Farming — Watching an active farming session
chunks.text:
Watching an active farming session


While farming is running, the page shows a live progress view instead of the tabs:

- An "active" section (title switches between "Farming (N)" while actually farming card drops, or
  "Building playtime (N)" while a game is still accumulating the playtime needed before it becomes
  farmable) — a grid of cards with cover art, a progress bar, and either an "N drops remaining"
  label or an "Xh / Yh until farmable" label depending on which phase that game is in.
- An "Up next (N)" list of games waiting their turn, each showing either "still accumulating
  playtime" progress or "Waiting its turn."
- A "Completed this session" list once any games finish — each row shows a checkmark for a normal
  completion (no drops left), or an info icon with an explanation for anything else: still inside
  Steam's refund window (with the date farming resumes), or removed from the whitelist for having
  no playtime / already having playtime.

Once a session ends, this view stays visible with a "Done" button at the bottom — dismissing it (or
starting a new session) is what actually clears it from view.

chunks.title: Card Farming — Settings
chunks.text:
Settings


Card Farming's settings tab (opened via the gear icon, or from the app's Settings modal) has:

- **Hours until farmable** — a number field for how much playtime a game needs before it's
  considered ready to farm (0 skips straight to farming).
- **Farm multiple games at once** (Beta badge) — a toggle to farm up to 32 games concurrently
  instead of one at a time; turning it on for the first time shows a one-time notice dialog warning
  that farming multiple games simultaneously can slow down how quickly cards drop per game.
- **Automatically farm cards** — a toggle that periodically checks for games with drops and starts
  farming them on its own; Gamer-tier only — on lower tiers this stays a real, clickable switch with
  a "GAMER" tier badge that opens the upgrade screen instead of turning on.
- **Skip refundable games** (Beta badge, agent-mode accounts only) — skip games still inside
  Steam's 14-day/under-2-hours refund window.
- **Skip unplayed games** and **Unplayed games only** — two mutually exclusive toggles (turning one
  on turns the other off).
- **Start another task when done** — a toggle that, when on, shows two buttons ("Achievement
  Unlocker" / "Auto Idle") to pick which automation starts automatically once farming finishes.

chunks.text:

chunks.title: Free Games — Page layout and header
chunks.text:
Page layout and header

subtitle, a circular refresh button, and a settings (gear) icon that opens Free Games' tab in the

chunks.title: Free Games — The game grid
chunks.text:
The game grid


Each card shows the game's thumbnail, name, and a "Claim" button. Clicking it claims that game for
your account — the button shows a loading state while in progress, then switches to a disabled
"Claimed" label once it succeeds. If the game turns out to already be owned, a small note appears

in red underneath instead. When there's nothing currently free, the page shows an empty state:

chunks.title: Free Games — Settings
chunks.text:
Settings

toggles:

  available on Steam. This is an app-wide setting, not tied to a specific account.

  without needing to visit this page. This is Gamer-tier only — on lower tiers it stays a real,
  clickable switch with a "GAMER" tier badge that opens the upgrade screen instead of turning on.

chunks.title: All Games (Games List) — Page layout and header
chunks.text:
Page layout and header


The header shows "Games", a "N games" count, a sort dropdown, and a circular refresh button. If
your Steam profile or game details appear to be private, a warning banner appears below the header
("Some game data may be missing — Your Steam profile or game details appear to be set to private,
so playtime, recently played, and some games may be incomplete.") with two buttons: "Change privacy

chunks.title: All Games (Games List) — Discovery carousels
chunks.text:
Discovery carousels

in settings): "Recommended" (games you own with zero playtime) and "Recently Played" (your
most-recently-played games, newest first). Cards inside a carousel behave exactly like library
cards below — the same idle toggle and achievements button work here too.

chunks.title: All Games (Games List) — The game grid, idling, and achievements
chunks.text:
The game grid, idling, and achievements


Below a "All Games" heading, every owned game appears as a card with its thumbnail, name, and two
small icon-only buttons: a play/stop icon that starts or stops idling that specific game (a live
timer overlays the thumbnail while it's idling), and a trophy icon that opens the Achievement
Manager overlay for that game. This is the only place idling is actually started or stopped by
picking individual games — the Idling page itself only shows a read-only, filtered view of whatever

chunks.text:
Global Search

screens don't show it at all, since a hidden affordance is clearer than one that looks clickable

chunks.title: Global Search — The titlebar search bar
chunks.text:
The titlebar search bar


On a wide window, this renders as a pill in the center of the titlebar reading "Search" (or your
current search text, with a small clear/X button once you've typed something). On a narrow window,
it collapses to a small circular search-icon button instead, to avoid colliding with the titlebar's
other buttons. Either form opens the same search modal when clicked.

chunks.title: Global Search — The search modal
chunks.text:
The search modal


A modal drops down from the top of the screen with a large search input (auto-focused) and a clear
button once you've typed anything. What shows below the input depends on what you've typed:

- **While typing** — up to 8 live-matching games from your library, each row showing the game's
  thumbnail and name. Clicking a row (or navigating to it with the arrow keys and pressing Enter)
  commits that name as your search text for whichever page you opened this from, and closes the
  modal. If nothing matches, it shows "No results found."
- **With nothing typed** — a "Recent searches" list of your past search terms instead, each with
  its own small remove button. If you have no recent searches, it shows "No recent searches."

Arrow keys move a highlight up and down through whichever list is showing; Enter commits the
highlighted row (or, if nothing's highlighted, your raw typed text). Escape clears the current text
without closing the modal first.

Committing a search only sets a filter on the page's own game list — it's local to whichever
feature you searched from (Games, Favorites, Card Farming, Achievement Unlocker, or Auto Idle all
filter their own "browse" tab; the curated list/queue tab on those pages is deliberately left
unfiltered).

The Idling page is a read-only, grouped view of whatever games are currently idling — it's not

page just shows the combined result and gives you a way to stop things in bulk.

chunks.title: Idling — Page layout and header
chunks.text:
Page layout and header


The header shows "Idling", a "N games idling" (or "No games idling") subtitle, and — only when at
least one game is idling — a red "Stop all" button that stops every idling game across every
feature at once.

chunks.title: Idling — Grouped sections
chunks.text:
Grouped sections


Currently-idling games are grouped into sections by whichever feature actually started them:
"Manually idled" (started directly from a game's card on the Games page), "Card Farming",
"Achievement Unlocker", "Auto Idle", or a generic "Other" bucket for anything that doesn't fit
those. Each section shows its own game count and, for every section except "Other", its own
"Stop" button that stops just that section's games (a red button next to the section title). Games

individually right from this page.

If a game happens to be claimed by more than one feature at once, it's shown under whichever
section has precedence, but "Stop all" still always covers it regardless of which section it's
displayed under.

Inventory Manager lets you browse your Steam Community inventory (trading cards, backgrounds,
emoticons, booster packs, sale items) and list items on the Steam Community Market, including
bulk actions for selling everything or just your duplicates.

chunks.title: Inventory Manager — Connecting first
chunks.text:
Connecting first


The first time you open this page (or whenever your Steam Community session needs
re-establishing), it shows a connect panel instead of any items — an "Automatic" tab (signs in to
Steam Community automatically, Gamer-tier only) and a "Manual" tab for pasting your own cookies
(available on every tier), plus a "Learn more" link.

chunks.title: Inventory Manager — Browsing and filtering your inventory
chunks.text:
Browsing and filtering your inventory


Once connected, a left-hand filter rail sits alongside the item grid: a search box, a "Sort by"
dropdown (name A-Z/Z-A, game A-Z/Z-A, badge level), and a "Filter" section with toggleable rows for
Trading cards, Foil, Backgrounds, Emoticons, Booster packs, On sale, Duplicates, Has badge, and
Locked — each with its own icon, and multiple can be active at once. An active filter row shows a
checkmark and a highlighted background.

Each item in the grid is its own card: a foil item gets a distinct holographic card background.
Every card has, top-left, a selection checkbox, and top-right, two small icon buttons — a lock icon
(toggles whether this item is protected from ever being sold automatically; a locked card dims to
half-opacity and its checkbox/price field become disabled) and a SteamCardExchange icon (opens that
item's page on steamcardexchange.net). Below the item's image is its name and, for trading cards,
its owning game name in green with a tooltip showing your badge level for that game (or that you
have no badge yet). At the bottom is a price input plus a small "list on the market" icon button
(disabled until a price is entered), and underneath that a "Fetch price" link that opens the price
order book for that item.

chunks.title: Inventory Manager — Checking the market price
chunks.text:
Checking the market price


Clicking "Fetch price" on a card opens a modal showing two tables side by side: "Sell orders" and
"Buy orders", each row showing a price and quantity. Clicking any row fills that price into the
item's price field and closes the modal — a fast way to price an item at a real current market
rate instead of typing one in by hand.

chunks.title: Inventory Manager — Bulk actions
chunks.text:
Bulk actions


The header shows the item count, and — once your inventory has loaded — four buttons:

- **"List selected (N)"** — lists every checked item at whatever price you've entered for it.
- **"Sell all (N)"** — fetches a market price for and lists every item currently shown (respecting
  active filters/search), using your price preference and sell-limit settings.
- **"Sell dupes"** — the same as Sell all, but scoped to duplicate copies only (keeping one copy of
  each item), ignoring locked items and active filters. This is Gamer-tier only — on lower tiers it
  stays a real, clickable (though dimmed) button with a "GAMER" badge that opens the upgrade screen
  instead of running.
- **"Remove listings"** (red) — cancels every active market listing for this account.

Each of these opens a confirmation dialog first, showing how many items are affected and an
estimated completion time, and warning to leave the app running until the process finishes.
Refresh and Settings (gear) buttons sit at the far right of the header.

chunks.title: Inventory Manager — Settings
chunks.text:
Settings


Inventory Manager's settings tab (opened via the gear icon, or from the app's Settings modal) has:

- **Currency** — a dropdown of ~35 Steam currencies to fetch prices and list items in.
- **Default price** — a two-button toggle for which price bulk-selling uses: "Highest buy order" or
  "Lowest sell order".
- **Price adjustment** — an amount added to every listing price, whether auto-filled or entered
  manually.
- **Sell limit** — a minimum and maximum price; only items priced within this range are ever
  listed.
- **Sell delay** — how many seconds to wait between listing each item, to avoid rate limiting.

chunks.title: Legacy (Local Steam Client) Sign-in Screen — Choosing an account
chunks.text:
Choosing an account


The card, titled "Choose an account", shows every Steam account currently saved on this device as a
row of square avatar tiles (your persona name underneath each). Clicking a tile selects it — the
selected tile's avatar gets a blue-to-violet gradient frame around it. If more accounts are saved

details couldn't be loaded, a warning banner appears above the tiles; if continuing with the chosen

chunks.text:
What happens on continue


Choosing "Continue" may switch which account the local Steam client itself is signed into (if it
wasn't already the one you picked) before finishing sign-in — a brief spinner replaces the whole
screen while this happens, then you're taken straight to the dashboard's games page.

category, and a scrollable content column on the right. Each category's content starts with a

chunks.title: Settings — General
chunks.text:
General


Shows an account header (avatar, display name, and either a Username or Steam ID field depending on
sign-in mode), then:

- **Language** — a dropdown to change the app's display language, with a "Help translate SGI" link
  to the project's Crowdin page.
- **Always online** (Legacy Sign-in accounts only) — periodically refreshes your Steam status so
  you don't appear away while idling.
- **Online status** and **Custom status while idling** (Steam Sign-in accounts only) — a dropdown
  of Steam presence states (Online, Busy, Away, Snooze, Looking to Trade, Looking to Play,
  Invisible, Offline), and a text field to replace the "Playing [game]" text friends see while
  idling with your own message. The status picker is free for everyone; the custom message field
  has its own "Save"/"Clear" buttons and is Gamer-tier only — on lower tiers those buttons still
  look normal but open the upgrade screen instead of saving (a "GAMER" badge sits next to the
  label).
- **Show games only** (Steam Sign-in accounts only) — hides DLC, soundtracks, videos, and tools
  from your library, showing only owned/family-shared games.
- **Run at startup**, **Start minimized**, **Close to tray** — three toggles controlling how the
  app launches and behaves when closed.
- **Automatically update games list** — silently refreshes your library in the background. Casual
  tier and above; below that it stays a real, clickable switch with a "CASUAL" badge that opens the
  upgrade screen instead of turning on.
- **Steam Web API key** — a password-style text field to override the app's built-in API key, with
  "Clear" and "Save" buttons.

chunks.title: Settings — Subscription
chunks.text:
Subscription


Shows your subscription status (a tier badge, billing email, and renewal or cancellation date) with
a "Manage subscription" button (opens your billing portal) and, for Casual subscribers, an
"Upgrade" button. Below that is a license key field: if you have one activated, it's shown masked
with "Copy" and "Clear" buttons; if not, there's an input to paste one and an "Activate" button.
Activating a key already active on another device shows a confirmation dialog first ("Transfer this
license key? — This license key is already active on another device. Activating it here will
deactivate it there.").

chunks.title: Settings — Customization
chunks.text:
Customization


Has toggles for "Disable tooltips" (hides hover tooltips app-wide) and showing/hiding the games
list's "Recommended" and "Recently Played" carousels — all free for everyone. Below that:

- **Font** — a dropdown of over 20 fonts, each previewed in its own typeface in the list.
- **Background image** — a "Choose image" button (opens a file picker for PNG/JPG/WEBP/GIF) and a
  "Clear" button.
- **Theme** — a row of small color swatches (Default, Blue, Red, Purple, Pink, Orange, Black,
  White) to pick as the app's color theme.

Font and Background are Casual-tier gated (a "CASUAL" badge appears next to their labels); Theme's
swatches are all visible and clickable regardless of tier, but selecting anything other than
Default on a lower tier opens the upgrade screen instead of applying it.

chunks.title: Settings — Steam Credentials
chunks.text:
Steam Credentials


Lets you save Steam Community cookies once so Card Farming and Inventory Manager don't need them
re-entered separately. For a Gamer-tier Steam Sign-in account, this shows a plain note instead:
"Not needed. This account signs in via Steam and gets its Steam Community session automatically."
Everyone else sees the same Automatic/Manual connect panel used on the Card Farming and Inventory
Manager pages, plus a "Learn more" link.

chunks.title: Settings — Game Settings
chunks.text:
Game Settings


A two-column layout: a searchable, scrollable list of every owned game on the left (a small dot
marks any game with a custom override), and fields on the right grouped into three bordered
sections — Playtime, Idling, and Achievement Unlocker. A toggle button next to the search box
filters the list to only customized games.

With no game selected, the right side shows account-wide defaults: "Max playtime (all games)" and
"Max idle time (all games)" (0 means unlimited). Selecting a game from the list switches to that
game's own overrides instead — "Max playtime", "Max idle time", and "Max achievement unlocks" for
that specific game, each overriding the account-wide value when set above 0. A note under each
section explains its scope (e.g. the idle-time cap doesn't apply to achievement unlocking, which
has its own separate cap).

chunks.title: Settings — Keybinds
chunks.text:
Keybinds


A read-only reference list (not an editor — no shortcut here can be remapped) of every keyboard
shortcut the app supports, grouped into "Zoom" (zoom in/out, reset zoom, with scroll-wheel
alternatives shown) and "Navigation" (next/previous page, open search, toggle settings, toggle
sidebar) sections.

chunks.title: Settings — Debug
chunks.text:
Debug


Shows the app version, OS, and whether this is a portable or installed build, followed by a row of
buttons: "View log file", "Open settings file", "Export settings" (copies your settings to the
clipboard), "Clear logs" (red), "Reset settings" (red), and "Clear data" (red). Below that is a
scrollable, monospace live view of the app's most recent log lines (error lines highlighted in
red).

"Reset settings" and "Clear data" both open a confirmation dialog before acting:
- **Reset settings** resets your Steam Web API key override and, if signed in, this account's
  achievement unlocker, inventory manager, card farming, and free games settings back to their
  defaults — your signed-in accounts stay signed in.
- **Clear data** signs every account out, stops any running automation, clears logs, and wipes
  locally-stored app data on this device (recent searches, inventory locks, etc.) — this can't be
  undone.

chunks.title: Sidebar — Sidebar
chunks.text:
Sidebar


This is source content for the AI Assistant's knowledge base (see `scripts/build-ai-corpus.mjs`),
generated by reading the actual `src/shared/components/dashboard/Sidebar.tsx` and
`SidebarItem.tsx` so the AI Assistant can describe exactly what a user sees and clicks, not just
what the feature does. Regenerate this file (via the `/generate-ui-guide sidebar` skill) whenever
this UI changes in a way that would make the description below inaccurate.

The sidebar is the app's main navigation, always visible on the left of every dashboard page. It
can be collapsed to a narrow icon-only rail (toggled from the titlebar's sidebar icon, or Ctrl+W) —
collapsed items show just their icon, with the label available as a hover tooltip instead.

chunks.title: Sidebar — Navigation sections
chunks.text:
Navigation sections


Three grouped sections, each with a small uppercase header (hidden while collapsed):

- **Games** — Games, Idling, Favorites, Free Games.
- **Automation** — Card Farming, Achievement Unlocker, Automatic Idler.
- **Misc** — Inventory Manager.

A nav item's icon pulses (and its label turns accent-colored) while that feature has something
actively running: Idling pulses while any game is idling, Card Farming while a farming cycle is
active, and Achievement Unlocker while it's running — so you can tell an automation is live from
anywhere in the app, not just its own page. Free Games' icon turns gold whenever there's at least
one unowned free game currently claimable.

chunks.title: Sidebar — Ads
chunks.text:
Ads


In production, non-Pro accounts see a small ad slot near the bottom of the sidebar, above the
footer. Subscribing removes it.

chunks.title: Sidebar — Footer
chunks.text:
Footer


At the bottom, above a divider:

- **Plan row** — shows your current tier ("Plan" label plus a tier badge). For Casual subscribers,
  this row is clickable and opens the upgrade screen scrolled to the Gamer tier; for Free and Gamer
  accounts it's a static label (Free's upsell lives in the titlebar's "Go Pro" pill instead, and
  Gamer has nothing higher to upgrade to). Hidden entirely while the sidebar is collapsed.
- **Account switcher and Settings** — the account switcher (avatar, name, and a chevron) sits next
  to a gear icon button that opens the Settings modal. See the account-switcher UI guide for what
  clicking the switcher does.

chunks.title: Sign-in Landing Page — Sign-in Landing Page
chunks.text:
Sign-in Landing Page


This is source content for the AI Assistant's knowledge base (see `scripts/build-ai-corpus.mjs`),
generated by reading the actual `src/features/sign-in-landing/` component code (plus the shared
`AuthLayout`/`SignInHero` chrome it renders inside) so the AI Assistant can describe exactly what a
user sees and clicks, not just what the feature does. Regenerate this file (via the
`/generate-ui-guide sign-in-landing` skill) whenever this feature's UI changes in a way that would
make the description below inaccurate.

This is the very first screen shown when the app launches with no account signed in (`/`), and also
the first step of the "Add another account" flow from the account switcher.

chunks.title: Sign-in Landing Page — Overall layout
chunks.text:
Overall layout


The screen splits into two columns. The left column shows the app logo (with a glowing cyan/violet
ring behind it) and the sign-in card itself. The right column shows a marketing panel: a headline
and subtitle over a continuously auto-scrolling wall of game cover art, with a screenshot of the
app layered on top. In the bottom-left corner, a language switcher sits next to a "Need help?" link
that opens the sign-in documentation page in your browser.

chunks.title: Sign-in Landing Page — Choosing a sign-in method
chunks.text:
Choosing a sign-in method


The card, titled "Sign in to Steam Game Idler", offers two buttons stacked vertically:

- **"Steam Sign-in"** (primary, filled) — the recommended method; doesn't require a local Steam
  client. Selecting it goes to the Steam Sign-in screen (username/password or QR code).
- **"Legacy Sign-in"** (secondary, outlined) — requires a real, currently-running local Steam
  client. Selecting it goes to the local account picker. This button is hidden entirely on Linux,
  which has no local-Steam-client sign-in path at all.

When shown inside "Add another account" (not the initial landing page), these buttons can be
restricted:
- If a local (CLI-mode) account is already signed in, "Legacy Sign-in" is a plain disabled button
  with a note underneath: "A local Steam client account is already signed in — only one can be
  signed in at a time."
- If you've hit your subscription tier's limit on concurrent Steam Sign-in accounts, "Steam
  Sign-in" either becomes a plain disabled button (if you're already on the highest tier) or stays
  a real, clickable, slightly dimmed button with a "GAMER" tier badge that opens the upgrade screen
  instead of starting sign-in — either way with an explanatory note underneath.

On the very first sign-in (not the "Add another account" flow), a footnote below the buttons reads:
"By continuing, you agree to the Terms of Service and acknowledge that you have read our Privacy
Policy," with both terms as clickable links opening the respective pages in your browser.

chunks.title: Titlebar — Titlebar
chunks.text:
Titlebar


This is source content for the AI Assistant's knowledge base (see `scripts/build-ai-corpus.mjs`),
generated by reading the actual `src/shared/components/titlebar/` component code (plus the
`UpdateButton`/`GoPro` buttons it mounts) so the AI Assistant can describe exactly what a user sees
and clicks, not just what the feature does. Regenerate this file (via the `/generate-ui-guide
titlebar` skill) whenever this UI changes in a way that would make the description below
inaccurate.

The titlebar spans the full width of the top of the window and is the app's only way to move,
minimize, maximize, or close it, since the window itself has no OS-drawn title bar. It's present on
every screen, including sign-in.

chunks.title: Titlebar — Left side
chunks.text:
Left side


Shows the app logo and "Steam Game Idler" wordmark, sized to match the sidebar's current width so
it stays visually anchored above it. On dashboard pages there's also a sidebar-toggle icon button
next to it (switches between an open and collapsed rail icon). A "Go Pro" pill appears here for
free-tier users only — an animated blue border, "Support Steam Game Idler" copy (hidden on narrow
windows), and a white "Go Pro" badge; clicking it opens the upgrade screen. Casual and Gamer
subscribers don't see this pill — their upgrade path is the "Plan" row in the sidebar instead.

chunks.title: Titlebar — Right side
chunks.text:
Right side


From left to right, when present:

- **Update button** — a circular down-arrow icon, shown only when an update is ready. Clicking it
  downloads and installs the update.
- **AI Assistant** — a robot icon (dashboard pages only) that opens the AI Assistant chat overlay.
  Visible to every tier — free-tier accounts just get a lower daily message cap, not a locked
  button.
- **Help Desk** — a headset icon that opens the live-chat support widget; a small red dot appears
  on it when there's an unread message. This button is Casual-tier and above only — it doesn't
  render at all on the free tier.
- **Notifications** — a bell icon with a red badge showing the unseen count. Clicking it opens a
  panel listing recent app notifications (each with a title, message, and relative timestamp), with
  a "Mark all as read" link at the top when there's anything to clear. An empty state reads "No
  notifications yet."
- **Menu** — a chevron-in-square icon opening a dropdown with: "Documentation", "Report an issue",
  "Feature request", "Join our Discord", "Changelog" (opens the changelog dialog), and — only on
  builds that support self-updating — "Check for updates".
- A vertical divider, then the three window controls: minimize, maximize/restore, and close (close
  turns red on hover).

chunks.title: Titlebar — Search bar
chunks.text:
Search bar


Below the main row, a global search bar spans the titlebar on pages that support it — see the
global-search UI guide for how that works.

chunks.title: Platform and sign-in differences — Platform and sign-in differences
chunks.text:
Platform and sign-in differences


This file is source content for the AI Assistant's knowledge base (see `scripts/build-ai-corpus.mjs`)
— a user-facing summary of behavior that genuinely differs by operating system or sign-in method.
Keep this free of internal implementation detail (module names, code paths); it should read like a
support article, not a developer doc.

chunks.title: Platform and sign-in differences — Windows and Linux support
chunks.text:
Windows and Linux support


Steam Game Idler runs on both Windows and Linux desktop, but with different capability levels:

- **Windows** supports both sign-in methods: Steam Sign-in (recommended) and Legacy Sign-in
  (fallback, requires a real local Steam client).
- **Linux** supports Steam Sign-in only. There is no Legacy Sign-in option on Linux at all — the
  sign-in screen simply doesn't show that button on Linux.

chunks.title: Platform and sign-in differences — Steam Sign-in vs. Legacy Sign-in
chunks.text:
Steam Sign-in vs. Legacy Sign-in


- **Steam Sign-in** (username/password or QR code) is the recommended way to sign in. It doesn't
  need a local Steam client installed or running at all.
- **Legacy Sign-in** is a fallback for users who prefer not to enter their Steam credentials into
  SGI. It requires a real, currently-running, signed-in local Steam client on the same machine.
  Windows only.

chunks.title: Platform and sign-in differences — Features that work differently depending on which one you use
chunks.text:
Features that work differently depending on which one you use


- **Game Coordinator titles** — Team Fortress 2, Dota 2, Counter-Strike 2, Left 4 Dead 2, and
  Portal 2 — are not supported for idling/achievements when signed in with Steam Sign-in. Use
  Legacy Sign-in (Windows only) for these specific games.
- **Idling** works differently under the hood: Legacy Sign-in idles one game per background
  process, while Steam Sign-in can idle up to 32 games from a single connection. In practice this
  just means Steam Sign-in has a higher idling limit.
- **Card Farming's automatic Steam cookie retrieval** works instantly and silently under Steam
  Sign-in. Under Legacy Sign-in, the first time it's needed, a small sign-in window appears since
  there's no other way to get a session.
- **Custom idle status message** (the text shown to friends instead of "Playing [game]") and the
  online status picker are only available when signed in with Steam Sign-in — there's no
  equivalent under Legacy Sign-in. An "Anti-AFK" feature exists for Legacy Sign-in instead, which
  keeps the local Steam client from showing you as away.
- Only one Legacy Sign-in account can be signed in at a time (a real Steam client can only be
  logged into one account). Multiple Steam Sign-in accounts can be signed in at once
  (concurrency limit depends on your subscription tier).

chunks.title: Platform and sign-in differences — Known Linux-only quirks
chunks.text:
Known Linux-only quirks


These are limitations of the underlying Linux desktop environment, not bugs in SGI:

- No rounded window corners (Windows gets this for free from Windows 11; Linux window managers
  don't do this automatically the same way).
- Clicking the system tray icon always opens the tray menu, rather than showing/hiding the window
  — this is how the Linux tray protocol works, there's no separate left-click behavior available.
- Occasionally an extra click is needed after dragging the title bar before other buttons respond
  — a known upstream issue in the underlying app framework on Linux.
- The tray's "Reset window position" option doesn't do anything on Linux — the Wayland display
  protocol doesn't allow apps to set their own window position.
- The AppImage build can feel slightly less smooth than the .deb/.rpm builds. If you're on Linux
  and performance matters to you, installing via .deb or .rpm (if your distro supports either) is
  recommended over the AppImage.
- Portable mode (running the app without installing it) is a Windows-only concept — every Linux
  package format installs normally and supports auto-updates.

chunks.title: Platform and sign-in differences — Subscription tiers and where they apply
chunks.text:
Subscription tiers and where they apply


Every core feature (Card Farming, Achievement Unlocker, Achievement Manager, Inventory Manager,
Free Games, Idling, Auto Idle, Favorites, Playtime Booster) is completely free and always will be.
PRO (Casual and Gamer tiers) unlocks convenience/automation extras on top — see the Pro comparison
table in the docs for exactly what each tier includes. A Pro subscription is tied to a license key,
not to any specific Steam account, and works the same regardless of whether you sign in with Steam
Sign-in or Legacy Sign-in.
